mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a kitchen addition and a kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen addition expands the physical footprint of your home outward, whereas an interior kitchen remodel reconfigures space within your existing walls. A remodel works well if your current square footage meets your needs and only requires updated cabinets, countertops, or layout changes. A full addition involves pouring a new foundation, framing exterior walls, roofing, and tying in utilities to create new floor area. While an addition provides significant space for large islands, walk-in pantries, or open-concept living, it involves exterior construction work, longer schedules, and higher investment than remodeling inside existing boundaries.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchen addition builds new square footage outward with new foundation and framing, while a remodel reconfigures finishes and layout within existing home walls.
